question.text: A plane electromagnetic wave, has frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> and its energy density is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> in vacuum. The amplitude of the magnetic field of the wave is close to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>πε</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>9</mn></msup><mfrac><msup><mi>Nm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> and speed of light <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
